newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - IRELAND - JULY 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - IRELAND - JULY 4.

text.p: Following are the highlights of Irish press on Friday:
- Briain will send thousands of troops to guard strategic locations throughout Northern Ireland this weekend if no agreement is reached on the route of the Drumcree Orange march.
- The public will soon be asked to inform on drivers who park illegally. A special "hot line" with its own free phone number will be in operation within weeks.
- Mackie, the publicly-quoted Belfast engineering group, is not aware of any current or pending investigation into recent developments at the company, according to new chief executive Sul Sahota.

- The Northern Ireland secretary, Mo Mowlam, was meeting security chiefs on the Drumcree crisis at Stormont Castle last night but hopes of a compromise were fading and a decision on the parade is now likely to be made on security grounds.

- The former Archbishop of Dublin, Dr John McQuaid, was alerted in 1960 that a priest convicted last week of sexual assault against two young girls had sent indecent photos involving two children to Britain to be developed.
- Former Transport minister Michael Lowry faces further tough questioning about his non-payment of tax on money paid to him by Dunnes stores when the payments-to-politicians resumes today.

-Relations between Prime Minister Bertie Ahern and Britain's Tony Blair have hit early choppy waters after Ahern's warning that the Orange Order march should not be forced down Portadown's Garvaghy Road on Sunday.
- Irish beaches are underpopulated because of the foul weather and life guards have found themsleves guarding against chill winds more than anything else.

- Women's groups reacted with horror last night to the disclosure that a rape victim had left the country because of death threats and ostracisation by sections of the county Kerry community in which she lives.
